name: Evelyn Atwood
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember saving a whole gang's signatures after a shutdown.” Sunday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Evelyn prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I know the hook in that W from the attendance board. Our best tallyman never learned joined-up writing.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cropped bottle-green coat and a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. Evelyn has a straight nose and deep-set eyes, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Evelyn looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
personality: Evelyn loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Evelyn remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To identify the chalk writer from a shared shift.
family: Lydia Macrae is Evelyn’s younger cousin. Evelyn asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Lydia chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The widow's dividend*, Lydia says, “I can't forgive the first owner's eviction of my aunt.”
connections: Dennis Shaw. One recognizes the chalk hand and the other recognizes its possible second language.

reactions.situation: A handwriting expert contradicts an old dock worker
reactions.response: Evelyn puts the expert's reading beside the dock worker's account and asks for the date of each.

reactions.response: Evelyn asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.
